entry.title: BC Time Zone Change Planning
entry.content:
Nov 16, 09:46 MST
Resolved - This incident has been resolved.

Oct 26, 16:17 MST
Update - If you are using UBC FASmail or UBC Student Email, you can now update your meetings using UBC IT's self-service tool. The tool can update many meetings automatically and identify those that require manual review.

If you are not using UBC FASmail or UBC Student Email, please consult with your department or organization on how to update your upcoming meetings. You may need to manually update your meetings to the new time zone.

For updated information, visit https://www.it.ubc.ca/timezonechange

Oct 20, 17:38 MST
Update - A guidance page has been developed to assist the UBC community in navigating the time zone change. This post will receive updates as more information becomes available. Further communications will be shared later this week.

https://it.ubc.ca/news/october-20-2026/bc-time-zone-change-what-it-means-your-calendar-and-devices

Oct 16, 15:18 MST
Update - UBC IT is still working with vendors and validating guidance. We plan to share detailed information on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 (afternoon).

Oct 9, 14:14 MST
Investigating - British Columbia has adopted permanent year-round daylight saving time (Pacific Time), with the change scheduled to take effect on November 1. We recognize that some community members may have questions about the impact on calendars, devices, and scheduled meetings.

UBC IT is actively working with Microsoft and Apple to coordinate the required time zone updates for computers, mobile devices, and calendaring services. We anticipate updates from our vendors will begin rolling out next week.

UBC IT plans to provide detailed guidance by October 16 outlining what to expect and any actions that may be required.
Thank you for your patience as we work to ensure a smooth transition.

entry.title: Microsoft announces removal of Office support for older systems and software versions, July 13, 2026
entry.content:
Nov 16, 09:44 MST
Resolved - This incident has been resolved.

Jul 10, 15:48 MST
Investigating - Microsoft has announced that effective July 13th, 2026, Office applications will no longer be supported on older MacOS and iOS systems, and further, they are removing support for older versions of Office entirely.

• Clients which are running operating systems earlier than the following minimums will no longer be able to edit or save files after the change:
Mac OS – minimum version 12.0 (Monterey)
iOS – minimum version 17.0

• Clients who are using Office 2019 for Mac, regardless of operating system, will be unable to edit or save files after the change.
• Clients who are using Office 2021 for Mac or MS 365 apps on iPhone and iPads will continue to function normally, provided the operating systems are supported (as listed above) and at the following minimum software versions:
Office 2021 for Mac – minimum version 16.83
MS365 apps for iOS – minimum version 2.93

UBC IT strongly recommends that all clients running Office on a Mac, iPhone, or iPad update their operating systems and Office software before July 13th to prevent any disruptions.

For more information, see https://ubc.service-now.com/kb_view.do?sysparm_article=KB0020043

entry.title: Canvas Zoom Integration Time Zone Issue
entry.content:
Nov 13, 08:44 MST
Resolved - This incident has been resolved.

Nov 3, 15:24 MST
Identified - We have identified an issue where Zoom meetings accessed through Canvas may show a start time that is one hour off, even when your Zoom timezone is set to “(GMT-7:00) Vancouver.”

This affects the displayed time only. If your meeting was created using the “(GMT-7:00) Vancouver” timezone, it is still scheduled at the correct time.

Workaround: To see the correct meeting times in Canvas, set your Zoom timezone to “(GMT-7:00) Arizona” when using Zoom through Canvas.

Nov 3, 11:55 MST
Update - Users accessing Zoom through Canvas may see meeting times shown in the wrong timezone. The timezone may also change on its own when the page is refreshed. We are currently investigating the issue.
In the meantime:
• When scheduling a new meeting, make sure the timezone is set to “(GMT -7:00) Pacific Time (Vancouver)” before saving.
• For meetings already scheduled, times in Canvas should display correctly as long as your Zoom timezone is set to “(GMT -7:00) Pacific Time (Vancouver).”

Nov 3, 10:24 MST
Investigating - We are currently investigating the time zone issue in Canvas Zoom integration. Users may notice inconsistent time zone displayed on the top of the web page. Please change to “(GMT-7:00) Vancouver” for correct time to join/schedule sessions.
